caveats: This is a model, not a forecast: the futures re-use real weather years with labelled adjustments.
Backtests score energy trading only. Ancillary services, ERCOT's ADER caps and NYISO's reserves are not modelled.
Today's observed weather stands in for a day-ahead forecast.
New York's lead rests on a capacity price that is an assumption; ERCOT contract values are assumptions too.

algorithms.name: Clockwork
algorithms.rule: Charges in the cheapest and discharges in the dearest fixed window of the last {CLOCK_DAYS} days' average day, every day, whatever the weather.
algorithms.ignores: Weather, gas and today's real prices.

algorithms.name: Forecaster
algorithms.rule: Forecasts tomorrow's price for every quarter hour from recent days, rescales the swings to a typical day, and plans with a dynamic programme: what is a stored kWh worth in each interval. Then it acts on each real price as it arrives.
algorithms.sees: Prices up to yesterday and the real price now.

algorithms.name: Weather-regime
algorithms.rule: Finds {ANALOGS} past days with weather, gas and recent prices like today's, plans for each as a full price path, and re-weights the paths through the day as real prices arrive. Holds a bigger backup before wind, flood-rain and hard-freeze days, and leaves heat days for selling.
algorithms.sees: Prices, today's weather, yesterday's gas price and the real price now.

algorithms.name: Spike hunter
algorithms.rule: Keeps the battery full. Buys only below the {SPIKE_LO} percentile of the last {SPIKE_WIN} days of prices and sells only above the {SPIKE_HI}. It trades rarely and earns the most per MWh sold.
algorithms.sees: Prices up to yesterday and the real price now.
algorithms.ignores: Weather, gas and the time of day.

algorithms.name: Adaptive learner
algorithms.rule: Runs every rule above, plus two variants, as shadow batteries and follows, zone by zone, whichever has earned the most lately, weighting each day further back by {LEARNER_GAMMA}. It switches only on a clear lead.
algorithms.sees: Everything the others see, and how each of them has done.
algorithms.ignores: Nothing; it decides only which rule to follow.

sitingRules.name: Last year's best
sitingRules.rule: Puts all of the next {SITE_MW} into last year's best option.

sitingRules.name: Trend
sitingRules.rule: Scores each option by its {SITE_A2_YEARS}-year mean plus half the trend, and puts no more than {SITE_A2_CAP} into one option in a year.

sitingRules.name: Risk-adjusted
sitingRules.rule: Scores each option by its {SITE_A3_YEARS}-year mean minus half its standard deviation, and splits the {SITE_MW} between the top three in shares of {SITE_A3_SHARES}.

sitingRules.name: Best year
sitingRules.rule: Scores each option by its single best year of the last {SITE_A4_YEARS}, and splits the {SITE_MW} between the top two in shares of {SITE_A4_SHARES}.

sitingRules.name: Recency-weighted posterior
sitingRules.rule: Weights the last {SITE_A5_YEARS} years, each older year counting {SITE_A5_DECAY} as much, scores by mean less a quarter of the standard deviation, and places one MW at a time. Trusts the latest year after a structural break.
